sections.heading: Introduction to Python
sections.content:
Python is a high-level, general-purpose, interpreted programming language created by Guido van Rossum in 1991.

Features of Python:
• Easy to learn — simple, readable syntax
• Interpreted — executed line by line
• Platform independent — runs on Windows, Mac, Linux
• Free and open source
• Extensive libraries (NumPy, Pandas, Django, etc.)

sections.heading: Your First Python Program
sections.content: Python programs are written in a text editor or IDLE (Python's built-in IDE) and saved as .py files.

codeBlocks.code:
# This is a comment
print('Hello, World!')   # Output: Hello, World!

# Taking input from user
name = input('Enter your name: ')
print('Hello,', name)
codeBlocks.explanation: The print() function displays output. The input() function reads a string from the keyboard.

sections.heading: Variables and Keywords
sections.content:
A variable is a named container that holds a value. Python has dynamic typing — no need to declare types.

Rules for variable names:
• Can contain letters, digits, underscore
• Must start with a letter or underscore
• Case-sensitive (name ≠ Name)
• Cannot be a Python keyword

Keywords (reserved words): and, as, assert, break, class, continue, def, del, elif, else, except, False, finally, for, from, global, if, import, in, is, lambda, None, nonlocal, not, or, pass, raise, return, True, try, while, with, yield

codeBlocks.code:
# Valid variable names
student_name = 'Asha'
_private = 42
camelCase = True

# Multiple assignment
x, y, z = 1, 2, 3
a = b = c = 0  # All point to the same value

# Check all keywords
import keyword
print(keyword.kwlist)
codeBlocks.explanation: Python allows multiple assignment in a single statement. Variables can hold any type of value.
